title: Jouhikko (bowed lyre)
summary: The jouhikko is a bowed lyre of Finland and Karelia. It is carved from a single block of wood in a flat trapezoid shape with a deep oval hole cut through it, and the player’s left hand reaches in behind the strings. Three strings of horsehair or gut run over a low bridge and are bowed with a short curved bow, giving a hushed, droning sound that suits old sung verses.
howToPlay: Three strings run over the block. Each lane marks a string and the place where it is stopped from behind.
A bead slides along the string to the spot. Press and bow as it lands.
Two strings carry the melody and one hums as a drone, so the sound stays close and low.
Learn the phrase by echo, then play it through with the pulse.
rules: The tune moves within a narrow range, a few notes at a time.
A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
Lines are written for this game in the style of the tradition.
heritageNote: The jouhikko accompanied sung verses and dances in the villages of Finland and Karelia. The flat carved block with the hand hole and the humming drone string are its signature.
